> **Figure 4.** Database and triage calls select 5,332 genes for the deep dive, which runs in three sequential stages, producing one validated record. (a) Every protein-coding gene is assessed by the five reference databases and, in parallel, by the two-stage triage agent. The union of the two inputs is trimmed of proteins represented by a single database that the triage agent also called high-confidence non-surface with localization to clear non-surface compartments (noted in the figure), leaving 5,332 genes for the deep dive. (b) The per-gene deep-dive pipeline runs in three sequential stages, producing one validated record. Stage 1, evidence retrieval: public databases build a candidate corpus, a per-paper Haiku 4.5 abstract triage selects papers worth fetching, open-access full text is recovered through a tiered fallback, and a Haiku 4.5 trim and Sonnet 4.6 selector yield per-protein evidence sets. Stage 2, block builders (Sonnet 4.6): builders draft the record's surface-evidence, surface-biology, and risk sections. Stage 3, synthesis (Sonnet 4.6): the synthesizer reads every section draft plus the Stage 1 evidence set, deterministic features, and the triage verdict, then writes the executive summary, structured filters, and confidence rationale. We therefore pair each record’s LLM synthesis and evidence ledger with seven precomputed deterministic features from public structural and orthology resources: membrane topology and ECD length with DeepTMHMM [(Hallgren et al., 2022)](https://www.zotero.org/google-docs/?OW40lC); predicted and experimental structures for the canonical protein, isoforms, close paralogs, and mouse and cynomolgus orthologs from AlphaFold DB [(Bertoni et al., 2026)](https://www.zotero.org/google-docs/?L5E1eF) and the PDBe, with orthology from Ensembl Compara [(Dyer et al., 2025; Vilella et al., 2009)](https://www.zotero.org/google-docs/?50CcDn); SURFACE-Bind predicted binding sites [(Balbi et al., 2026)](https://www.zotero.org/google-docs/?hSdHXf); and predicted homo-oligomerization [(Schweke et al., 2024)](https://www.zotero.org/google-docs/?GP5brk). This lets a reader separate literature-derived calls from sequence-derived ones. The structured tags make this information queryable rather than buried in prose. For example, SRC is an inner-leaflet kinase that two databases (GO, HPA) score as surface on the strength of membrane association. Our record returns it as surface but tags it high state-dependence (disease-induced), direct-but-single-method evidence (either a single method type or from a single source), and a lysosomal-exocytosis mechanism, separating a genuine but conditional surface event from constitutive surface localization [(Delaveris et al., 2026)](https://www.zotero.org/google-docs/?KRCvZv). CD63, on the other hand, is called surface by four of five databases, but our record flags it as mostly intracellular: at rest it sits in lysosomes and reaches the surface mainly through activation-induced exocytosis, making it a weak standalone surface target, yet potentially a credible target for bispecific approaches where endolysosomal delivery is desirable [(de Goeij et al., 2016)](https://www.zotero.org/google-docs/?RCy3dx). Because every attribute is a queryable field, a user can filter the database at their own evidence threshold and context definition — for example restricting to direct multi-method evidence, or to state-independent surface presentation — rather than inheriting a single curator's definition. A database built by reading the literature is bounded by how much of it an agent can reach, so we audited reachability directly on a random sample of the discovery corpus. Discovery from 100 randomly selected proteins returned a median of 234 candidate papers per protein; from these we sampled 10 of their discovered papers each and attempted full-text recovery. 89% were recoverable, most through PubMed Central (88%; Figure S10). ### The deep dive yields a confidence-tiered and configurable
